newsitem.title: UK: Gold resurfaces above $340 but prospects clouded.
newsitem.headline: Gold resurfaces above $340 but prospects clouded.

text.p: Gold managed to struggle back above a technical threshold at $340.00 an ounce on Wednesday but sentiment remained bearish and dealers saw a prospect of a renewed slide back towards recent 1997 lows around $336.00.
Early trades featured Middle Eastern demand which helped gold fix $1.20 higher at $340.45 an ounce, but professional dealers still shunned the metal, staying short against further price drops.
"There is good support at $340 but my gut feeling is that this is just a respite...a bit of correction," said one dealer. "It will go lower. You've still got that overhang of central bank selling."
Revived fears that central banks may make new sales of gold had depressed bullion to a London morning fix on Tuesday at $338.95.
Bargain-hunting and industrial offtake lifted silver early, but it too faced the bleak prospect of digging for new lows, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium treaded a narrow range while continued delays in the Russian exports provided support.
Gold's physical offtake below $340 was encouraging and the market also benefitted from dollar's softer tone after mild U.S. data suggested the Federal Reserve may not hike interest rates on May 20.
Further such clues from the U.S. first quarter GDP figures due at 1230 GMT could stir up some demand for gold, but the overall outlook was clouded by concerns about central bank selling.
"The attitude (of central banks) towards gold has changed. That's why I don't see any fundamental reason to buy gold," said precious metals analyst Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corporation.

Gold was poised to test the February 12 low of $336.15 in the near term, but support was quite fragile and so further losses to the next technical level of $325 -- a four-year low -- could be foreseen.
Silver whipped under $4.70 after emerging from this week's earlier plunge to $4.59 once the supportive over-the-counter options expired on Monday.
Dealers said silver could plough through $4.70 but as in gold, the outlook remained gloomy signalling a test of support at $4.50 and below.
Platinum rose $1.00 to $373.50/$374.50 while palladium pared earlier gains and stood 75 cents lower at $156.50/$157.50.
Analysts predicted the white metals to stay in a rollercoaster range as long as the issue over delayed Russian supplies was unresolved. Shipments have stopped since December.
